gen-dafont-redux-gf-ovo: Ovo reads as a text serif with generous gaps at its curve endings and barely any thinning. Redux, the heading, spreads its wide-set letters out and swoops dramatically into every curve, so give the body text a size that lets its large middle band breathe.
gen-dafont-sf-wonder-comic-gf-domine: Domine reads dignified and compact, with a classic serif's short ascenders and open bowls. SF Wonder Comic crowds its words dense in the middle and leaves bowls unfinished, so Domine's slight pinch at each joint steadies the page beneath it.
gen-dafont-sf-wonder-comic-gf-esteban: Bold, dense, a little unfinished. Esteban, a serif with oversized lowercase and a wide-open e, gives SF Wonder Comic's half-closed bowls somewhere calm to land, since its thin strokes barely trail the stems.
gen-dafont-sf-wonder-comic-gf-faustina: SF Wonder Comic leaves one side of its bowls unfinished, which gives every word a striking, dense look. And Faustina, a text serif with pliers-jawed c shapes and gracefully thinning bowls, supplies the steady authority underneath.
gen-dafont-sf-wonder-comic-gf-halant: Halant opens the page with a faint thick-thin shift and outward-pointing terminals on a very large x-height. SF Wonder Comic does the loud work, dense words and half-open bowls, while Halant, a text serif, handles the quieter job of carrying text.
gen-dafont-sf-wonder-comic-gf-lisu-bosa: Lisu Bosa is a classic serif whose counters spill into the space around them, making each word look sturdy and large. Over many lines it would read steadily, with gentle spring-like contrast.
gen-dafont-sf-wonder-comic-gf-marcellus-: Marcellus SC reads literary and dignified, with gently modulated strokes and terminals pulled well back. And SF Wonder Comic, dense and striking above it, gives that restraint something bold to sit under.
gen-dafont-sf-wonder-comic-gf-montagu-sl: SF Wonder Comic packs its words dense and leaves its bowls open on one side, which makes a striking headline. But Montagu Slab, a classic serif with sturdy downstrokes and a generous x-height, is the one built for sustained reading.
gen-dafont-starborn-gf-faustina: Starborn scatters wide gulfs of space between letters, with a dark, thick band of lowercase through each line. And Faustina, a text serif with gracefully thinning bowls, grounds that dreaminess in something authoritative.
gen-dafont-starborn-gf-hedvig-letters-se: Dreamy and spaced-out, then grounded. Starborn is best at ethereal, widely spaced display lines, while Hedvig Letters Serif is best at sturdy, open-curved text with the soft thick-thin shift of a pencil.
